'''Lonnie Terrence Walker IV'''<ref>{{cite web |title=Lonnie Terrence Walker IV (USA) - Basketball Stats, Height, Age |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/players/226160-lonnie-terrence-walker-iv |website=FIBA Basketball |access-date=8 May 2026}}</ref> (born December 14, 1998) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Ligat HaAl]] and the [[EuroLeague]]. [[high school]], he was named [[Mr. and Miss Pennsylvania Basketball|Mr. Pennsylvania Basketball]] and earned [[McDonald's All-American]] honors. Walker played [[college basketball]] for the [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami Hurricanes]].

After being named to the all-freshman team in the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC), he was selected in the first round of the [[2018 NBA draft]] by the [[San Antonio Spurs]] with the 18th overall pick. He played four seasons with the Spurs before signing with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. He has also played for the [[Brooklyn Nets]] and the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].

==Early life==
Walker was born December 14, 1998, in [[Reading, Pennsylvania]]. He attended [[Reading Senior High School]] in Reading.<ref name=borzello_11172016/> Walker made his varsity basketball debut as a freshman and played 27 games averaging eight points per game, and later as a sophomore he averaged 16.9 points per game in a short season due to injury. In 29 games, as a junior, he averaged 17.1 points per game.

During his senior year, Walker was named a [[McDonald's All-American]] and voted [[Mr. Pennsylvania Basketball]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2017 McDonald's All-American Game boys rosters announced|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/-c4H_udHpk68Wy2LGvrS3Q/2017-mcdonald’s-all-american-game-boys-rosters-announced.htm|work=maxpreps|date=January 15, 2017|access-date=February 20, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Reading's Lonnie Walker caps high school career with Mr. PA Basketball honor|date=May 27, 2017|work=The Patriot-News|url=https://www.pennlive.com/highschoolsports/article/readings-lonnie-walker-caps-high-school-career-with-mr-pa-basketball-honor/|access-date=May 9, 2023}}</ref> He averaged a career best 18.4 points per game and surpassed Reading High grad and former NBA player [[Donyell Marshall]]'s school record in points by finishing with 1,828 total points scored. On March 25, 2017, Walker led Reading Senior High School to their first state championship in the program's 117-year history in a 64–60 win over the [[Pine-Richland High School|Pine-Richland Rams]]. Walker finished the game with 22 points, eight rebounds, four steals, and three assists.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Erdman|first1=Trey|url=http://rawsports.tv/wp/reading-high-are-the-state-champs-for-the-first-time-ever-by-trey-erdman/|title=Reading high are the state champs for the first time ever!!|website=rawsports.tv|access-date=October 31, 2024|date=March 26, 2017}}</ref>

During the season, Walker signed with the [[Miami Hurricanes]], passing on other scholarship offers from [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]], [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], [[Syracuse University|Syracuse]], and [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]].<ref name=borzello_11172016>{{cite web|first=Jeff|last=Borzello|title=Five Star Recruit Lonnie Walker commits to Miami Hurricanes|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/18062752/five-star-recruit-lonnie-walker-commits-miami-hurricanes|website=ESPN.com|date=November 17, 2016|access-date=February 20, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Lonnie Walker recruiting profile|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/207877/lonnie-walker|website=ESPN.com|access-date=February 20, 2017}}</ref>

==College career==
[[File:Lonnie Walker IV (cropped).jpg|thumb|Walker in 2017]]
Walker made his collegiate debut with the [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami Hurricanes]] on November 10, 2017, recording 10 points and a season-high five assists coming off the bench in a 77–45 blowout win over [[Gardner-Webb University]]. He created new highs of 12 points and 5 rebounds on December 2 in an 80–52 blowout win against [[Princeton University]] before recording season-highs of 26 points and 7 rebounds during his first collegiate [[starting lineup|start]] three days later in a 69–54 win over [[Boston University]]. Against [[Louisville]], he scored a game-high 25 points including an acrobatic layup in traffic to force overtime. In a game against [[Boston College]], he hit a [[3-pointer]] with two seconds remaining to win 79–78.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400986278|title=Walker's 3 pointer lifts Miami past Boston College 79–78|website=ESPN.com|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|access-date=February 24, 2018|date=February 24, 2018}}</ref> Walker finished the season averaging 11.5 points per game and was named to the [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] all-freshman team.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kaufman |first1=Michelle |title=One and done: UM's Walker enters NBA Draft |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/college/acc/university-of-miami/article207974329.html |website=Miami Herald |access-date=October 31, 2024 |date=April 4, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://theacc.com/news/2018/3/4/mens-basketball-acc-announces-all-conference-team-postseason-awards.aspx?path=mbball|title=ACC Announces All-Conference Team, Postseason Awards|website=TheACC.com|publisher=[[Atlantic Coast Conference]]|access-date=March 4, 2018|date=March 4, 2018}}</ref>

After his sole season with Miami concluded, Walker declared for the [[2018 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Cross |first1=Ken |title=Miami Basketball: Lonnie Walker leaves for draft; 'Canes roster could shuffle |url=http://collegehoopswatch.com/2018/04/07/miami-basketball-lonnie-walker-leaves-for-draft-canes-roster-could-shuffle/ |website=collegehoopswatch.com |access-date=October 31, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612232616/http://collegehoopswatch.com/2018/04/07/miami-basketball-lonnie-walker-leaves-for-draft-canes-roster-could-shuffle/ |archive-date=June 12, 2018 |date=April 7, 2018}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===San Antonio Spurs (2018–2022)===
On June 21, 2018, Walker was selected with the 18th overall pick by the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in the [[2018 NBA draft]]. Walker was later included in the 2018 [[NBA Summer League]] roster of the Spurs.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-announce-2018-utah-summer-league-roster|title=Spurs announce 2018 Utah Summer League roster|date=June 28, 2018|work=NBA.com|access-date=June 28, 2018}}</ref> On July 11, 2018, the Spurs announced that they signed Walker.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-sign-2018-first-round-pick-lonnie-walker-iv|title=Spurs sign 2018 first round pick Lonnie Walker IV|date=July 11, 2018|work=NBA.com|access-date=July 11, 2018}}</ref> On October 6, 2018, Walker was revealed to have a right medial meniscus tear.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2018/10/06/spurs-lonnie-walker-suffers-medial-meniscus-tear|title=Spurs rookie Lonnie Walker IV to have surgery for medial meniscus tear|date=October 6, 2018|work=NBA.com|access-date=October 6, 2018}}</ref> On November 25, 2018, the San Antonio Spurs assigned Walker the first time of the season to the [[Austin Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/san-antonio-assigns-lonnie-walker-iv-austin-spurs|title=San Antonio assigns Lonnie Walker IV to Austin Spurs|date=November 25, 2018|work=NBA.com|access-date=November 25, 2018}}</ref> Walker made his NBA debut on January 3, 2019, in a 125–107 win against the [[Toronto Raptors]], scoring three points and grabbing one rebound in five minutes of play.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fox43.com/article/sports/high-school/fan-of-the-night/reading-native-lonnie-walker-makes-nba-debut/521-cf2b3350-b8ce-4e74-915f-2c6e99165748|title=Reading native Lonnie Walker makes NBA debut|first=Cale|last=Ahearn|website=FOX43.com|publisher=[[WPMT]]|date=January 4, 2019|access-date=October 31, 2024}}</ref>

On December 3, 2019, Walker scored a career-high 28 points, including 19 in the 4th quarter, in a 135–133 double overtime win over the [[Houston Rockets]] with four rebounds, three steals and a block.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160945|title=Walker lifts Spurs; Rockets fall in 2OT despite Harden's 50|date=December 4, 2019|website=ESPN.com|access-date=December 4, 2019}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Lakers (2022–2023)===
[[File:Lonnie Walker 2023.jpg|thumb|right|Walker signs an autograph while with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in 2023]]
On July 6, 2022, Walker signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] on a one-year, $6.5M contract.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lakers to sign Lonnie Walker IV to 1-year deal |url=https://www.nba.com/news/lonnie-walker-2022-nba-free-agency |access-date=2022-07-12 |website=nba.com |date=July 6, 2022}}</ref> He began the [[2022–23 Los Angeles Lakers season|2022–23 season]] playing in 32 games, all starts, before being sidelined beginning in late December with knee [[tendinitis]].<ref name=turner_01292023>{{cite web|first=Broderick|last=Turner|title=Anthony Davis has idea about missed calls: Refs getting fined|date=January 29, 2023|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/lakers/story/2023-01-29/anthony-davis-lakers-boston-celtics-takeaways|access-date=May 9, 2023}}</ref><ref name=turner_05082023>{{cite web|first=Broderick|last=Turner|title=Lonnie Walker IV looking to make more contributions for Lakers in Game 4|date=May 8, 2023|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/lakers/story/2023-05-08/los-angeles-lakers-golden-state-warriors-game-4-preview|access-date=May 9, 2023}}</ref> At the time, he was averaging 14.7 points in 29.8 minutes per game and shooting 45.5% from the field and 38.9% on 3-pointers.<ref name=turner_05082023/> He seemed to be the Lakers top scorer after [[LeBron James]], [[Anthony Davis]], and [[Russell Westbrook]].<ref name=murray_05082023/> Walker returned after missing 14 games,<ref name=turner_01292023/> but his playing time was limited with the development of [[Austin Reaves]] and particularly after the Lakers acquired [[D'Angelo Russell]], [[Malik Beasley]], [[Jarred Vanderbilt]], and [[Rui Hachimura]] before the trade deadline.<ref name=turner_05082023/><ref name=murray_05082023>{{cite web|first=Law|last=Murray|title=Lonnie Walker IV, the Lakers' 'X-factor,' will keep staying ready for his playoff moments|date=May 8, 2023|work=The Athletic|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4496918/2023/05/08/lonnie-walker-lakers-warriors/|url-access=subscription|access-date=May 9, 2023}}</ref> After playing in a bit shy of 28 minutes through the first eight games of the [[2023 NBA playoffs|2023 playoffs]], Walker returned to the rotation and scored 12 points in 25 minutes in a 127–97 win over [[Golden State Warriors|Golden State]], giving the Lakers a 2–1 series lead in the conference semifinals.<ref name=turner_05082023/> In Game 4, he scored all 15 of his points in the fourth quarter to help the Lakers overcome a seven-point deficit and win 104–101.<ref>{{cite web|first=Dan|last=Woike|title=Lakers beat Warriors in a Game 4 thriller, now one win from conference finals|date=May 8, 2023|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/lakers/story/2023-05-08/los-angeles-lakers-golden-state-warriors-game-4-playoff-recap|access-date=May 9, 2023}}</ref>  In the 2022–23 season, in 56 games he averaged 23.2 minutes, 11.7 points, 1.9 rebounds, and 1.1 assists  per game while shooting 86% from the free throw line.<ref name=gm/>

===Brooklyn Nets (2023–2024)===
On July 10, 2023, Walker signed a reported one-year contract with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Lonnie Walker IV|date=July 10, 2023|work=NBA.com|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-sign-lonnie-walker-iv|access-date=July 11, 2023}}</ref>  In the 2023–24 season, in 54 games he averaged 17.4 minutes, 9.7 points, 2.2 rebounds, and 1.3 assists  per game while shooting 40% from three-point range and 83% from the free throw line.<ref name=gm/> On June 29, 2024, Walker said after the season finale he was unsatisfied with the disrespect he received from the Brooklyn Nets' coaching staff and became a free agent after the season.

On August 28, Walker signed a reported one-year contract with the [[Boston Celtics]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Celtics add free agent Walker on 1-year contract|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/41034335/free-agent-lonnie-walker-iv-joins-celtics-1-year-deal|website=ESPN.com|date=August 29, 2024|access-date=August 29, 2024}}</ref> but was waived on October 19.<ref>{{cite web|title=Boston Celtics Reportedly Release 6-Year NBA Player|url=https://www.si.com/fannation/nba/fastbreak/boston-celtics-reportedly-release-6-year-nba-player-lonnie-walker|website=SI.com|date=October 19, 2024|access-date=October 19, 2024}}</ref>

===Žalgiris Kaunas (2024–2025)===
On October 30, 2024, Walker signed with [[BC Žalgiris|Žalgiris Kaunas]] of the [[Lietuvos krepšinio lyga|Lithuanian Basketball League]] (LKL) and the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Gillingham|first=Geoff|title=Lonnie Walker joins Zalgiris|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/news/lonnie-walker-joins-zalgiris-kaunas/|website=EuroLeague|date=October 31, 2024|access-date=November 4, 2024}}</ref> He helped Žalgiris win the [[King Mindaugas Cup]], the top domestic cup competition, on February 16, 2025. In the 2024–2025 season, in 33 games he averaged 20.6 minutes, 13.5 points, 2.9 rebounds, and 2.0 assists  per game while shooting 40% from three-point range and 83% from the free throw line.<ref name=gm>[https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Lonnie-Walker/Summary/88916 "Lonnie Walker Player Profile,"] realgm.</ref>

On February 19, he parted ways with the team in order to return to the NBA.<ref>{{cite web |title=Į NBA išvykstantis L.Walkeris IV palieka "Žalgirį" |url=https://zalgiris.lt/naujienos/i-nba-isvykstantis-l-walkeris-iv-palieka-zalgiri |website=Žalgiris |access-date=February 20, 2025 |date=February 19, 2025}}</ref>

=== Philadelphia 76ers (2025) ===
On February 21, 2025, Walker signed with his hometown team, the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lonnie Walker IV Signed by the Sixers |url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/76ers-sign-lonnie-walker-iv |access-date=2025-02-21 |website=www.nba.com |language=en}}</ref> He made 20 appearances (seven starts) for Philadelphia, recording averages of 12.4 points, 3.2 rebounds, and 2.5 assists while shooting 80% from the free throw line. After the {{nbay|2024|end}} NBA season, the 76ers declined to exercise their team option on Walker's contract, making him an unrestricted free agent.<ref>{{Cite web |title=76ers decline Lonnie Walker IV's option for upcoming season |url=https://www.si.com/nba/76ers/news/76ers-decline-lonnie-walker-iv-option-for-upcoming-campaign-01jyyfx6kgez |website=SI.com |date=2025-07-01 |access-date=2025-07-24 |language=en}}</ref>

=== Maccabi Tel Aviv (2025–2026) ===
On July 24, 2025, Walker signed a two-year contract with [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]] and the [[EuroLeague]]. The contract is worth approximately $5 million gross. The deal includes NBA exit clauses for 2025, and 2026.<ref>{{cite web | last=Urbonas | first=Donatas | title=Lonnie Walker's salary in EuroLeague revealed | website=basketnews.com | date=2025-07-24 | url=https://basketnews.com/news-228376-lonnie-walkers-maccabi-deal-contract-value-and-nba-exit-clauses-revealed.html | access-date=2025-12-09}}</ref>  In the 2025–26 season, in 45 games he averaged 21.8 minutes, 15.2 points, 2.5 rebounds, and 2.2 assists  per game while shooting 40% from three-point range and 83% from the free throw line.<ref name=gm/>

==Personal life==
Walker is the son of Lonnie Walker III who moved from [[New Jersey]] to [[Reading, Pennsylvania]], to play basketball at [[Alvernia University]].<ref name=uggetti>{{cite web |last1=Uggetti |first1=Paolo |title=Lonnie Walker IV Is Out of This World |url=https://www.theringer.com/nba/2018/6/19/17477536/lonnie-walker-iv-draft-feature |website=The Ringer |access-date=May 9, 2023 |date=June 19, 2018}}</ref> Walker III dropped out of university when Walker IV was born in 1998 and he had to raise his son as a [[single parent]] while working multiple jobs.<ref name=uggetti /><ref name=orsborn>{{cite web |last1=Orsborn |first1=Tom |title=Father's influence led to Spurs' Lonnie Walker IV's passion for reading |url=https://www.expressnews.com/sports/spurs/article/Father-s-influence-led-to-Spurs-Lonnie-15033381.php |website=San Antonio Express-News |access-date=May 9, 2023 |date=February 6, 2020}}</ref> Walker IV was encouraged to read after school by his father and maintains reading as part of his pregame ritual.<ref name=orsborn />

Walker has a dog named Zola (named after [[Arnim Zola|the evil robot with the same name]]), who appeared with him in a [[People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals|PETA]] ad campaign, reminding people not to leave their dogs in hot, parked cars.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Lynch |first1=David |title=Spurs' Lonnie Walker reminds you not to leave your dogs in hot cars in PETA partnership |url=https://www.kens5.com/article/sports/nba/spurs/spurs-lonnie-walker-reminds-you-not-to-leave-your-dogs-in-hot-cars-in-peta-partnership/273-a9c5fdfd-74bb-48cf-a3da-27ac2a31cfbe |website=kens5.com |access-date=October 31, 2024 |date=July 11, 2019}}</ref>

In June 2020, Walker revealed he had been the victim of [[sexual abuse]] by family members as an adolescent, and had grown out his trademark long hairstyle as a coping mechanism. In deciding to cut his hair, Walker described the act as having "shed my skin mentally, emotionally, physically and spiritually."<ref>{{cite web |last1=McMenamin |first1=Dave |title=Spurs' Lonnie Walker IV says new haircut freeing as he works through childhood sexual abuse |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/29300594/spurs-lonnie-walker-iv-says-new-haircut-freeing-works-sexual-abuse |website=ESPN.com |date=June 12, 2020 |access-date=June 12, 2020}}</ref>
